title: Understanding Matrix Dimensions
text: In an OLS model, the matrix X is an $$n$$ by $$p+1$$ matrix, where $$n$$ is the number of observations and $$p+1$$ is the number of features including the intercept. The matrix $$X^T$$ is the transpose of X, making it a $$p+1$$ by $$n$$ matrix. Therefore, $$X^T$$ X results in a $$p+1$$ by $$p+1$$ matrix. Does this match the dimensions given in the problem?

title: Matrix Multiplication Dimensions
text: To determine the dimensions of $$X^T$$ X, consider the dimensions of X and $$X^T$$. If X is an $$n$$ by $$p+1$$ matrix, what are the dimensions of $$X^T$$?

title: Resulting Matrix Dimensions
text: Given that $$X^T$$ is a $$p+1$$ by $$n$$ matrix and X is an $$n$$ by $$p+1$$ matrix, what are the dimensions of the resulting matrix when you multiply $$X^T$$ by X?

title: Final Check
text: Now that you know the dimensions of $$X^T$$ X are $$p+1$$ by $$p+1$$, compare this with the statement in the problem. Is the statement correct?
